newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S CORK CONFIDENT AFTER INJURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S CORK CONFIDENT AFTER INJURY.

text.p: Injured key England fast bowler Dominic Cork said on Monday he was hopeful of being fit for the first cricket test against New Zealand starting on Friday.
Cork damaged his lower back on Sunday while bowling against Northern Districts. An X-ray on Monday showed no bone fracture and the injury was believed to be a soft-tissue problem.
"I feel a lot better today," said Cork, who has taken 67 wickets in 16 tests.
"It's an injury I haven't had any problem with before, and hopefully in a couple of days it'll go away and I'll be ready for Friday, if selected."
Cork tore through New Zealand's opening batsmen on Saturday, when he removed Northern Districts test pair Bryan Young and Blair Pocock in 16 balls.
England beat Northern Districts by 10 wickets in their second four-day cricket tour match in New Zealand.
